newsitem.title: UK: ICI sells polyester business to DuPont.
newsitem.headline: ICI sells polyester business to DuPont.

text.p: Imperial Chemical Industries Plc said on Monday it had agreed to sell its polyester polymer, titanium dioxide and polyester film businesses to DuPont Co for $3 billion.
In a statement, ICI said the deal would be "earnings enhancing" for the company and confirmed a decisive strategic shift in the ICI portfolio. It would also significantly reduce ICI's borrowings.

"After the recent acquisition of the former Unilever Speciality Chemicals businesses, this series of disposals confirms the decisive shift in ICI's portfolio," ICI chief executive Charles Miller Smith said.
"The transactions represent real value for ICI and its shareholders."
The businesses to be sold to DuPont contributed aggregate sales of 1.45 billion pounds and a trading profit of 17 million in 1996. At end-1996 they had aggregate net assets of 1.12 billion pounds.
The businesses sold to DuPont are as follows:
Polyester polymer and intermediates for a consideration of $1.6 billion
Titanium dioxide (excluding north America) for a consideration of $750 million.
Polyester film for a consideration of $650 million

ICI said it was developing options for the disposal of its North American titanium dioxide businesses. DuPont has agreed that if the proceeds to ICI from the sale of these are less than $150 million, DuPont will cover any deficit.
ICI said it has anticipated the disposals will create a small profit over book value before the write-off of purchased goodwill in tioxide of 130 million pounds.
